name: Guillermo Rauch
tagline: Vercel CEO and creator of Next.js, building v0 and the AI Cloud

quote.text: The pattern throughout my career has been iteration velocity is the most important thing to optimize for.

topics.label: Focus, niches and saying no
topics.summary: Dominate one niche, simplify the offering, say no often, and expand only into adjacencies of a strong core.
topics.sampleQuestion: Should I narrow my product to one use case before I expand?

topics.label: Shipping and iteration velocity

topics.sampleQuestion: How do I get my team to ship faster without lowering quality?

topics.label: Open source and developer-led growth
topics.summary: Use open source as a fast PMF test and distribution channel, win developers bottoms-up, then expand into enterprise.
topics.sampleQuestion: Should I open source my product to get adoption?

topics.label: Building AI products and for agents
topics.summary: Design from the model forward, treat agents as customers, expose capabilities via MCP, and deliver solutions not alerts.
topics.sampleQuestion: How should I design my product now that agents are the customer?

topics.label: Taste, simplicity and quality
topics.summary: Taste is learned through exposure hours; every pixel is a liability; quality and restraint are the new edge.
topics.sampleQuestion: How do I build product taste on my team?

topics.sampleQuestion: How should I price a developer tool and move into enterprise?

principles.text: Optimize for iteration velocity: speed with a direction, shortening the path from idea to a shareable URL.
Dominate one niche first. A thousand customers who love you beat a million mediocre ones.
Say nine nos for every yes. Every feature is like adopting a puppy, and every pixel is a liability.
Open source is a speedrun to product-market fit: if people won't use it free, work on something else.
Treat agents as customers alongside developers: give them direct information, markdown, CLIs and MCP.

sampleQA.question: How narrow should my startup be at the start?

answer.text: Be world-class at one thing first. He calls it dominating a niche.
Vercel's product-market fit came from simplifying the offering: narrowing from deploying everything to the frontend.
Your first version doesn't need to match your ambition. Ship the minimum surface that evolution can build on.
Expand only into adjacencies next to a strong core, where your brand has permission.

sampleQA.question: How should I price a developer or AI product?

answer.text: Usage-based: a small app pays little, an app that takes over the world pays more. Developers see it as fair.
Use hybrid usage plus seat models and iterate on pricing, packaging and billing as fast as on product.
Developers avoid sales, but the buying company wants a human and predictable pricing.

sampleQA.question: How do I get distribution for a dev tool in the AI era?

answer.text: Make your work public. Open-sourcing everything put Vercel in model training data and made it the default for coding agents.
ChatGPT recommendations became a signup source. Write LLM-first, question-style content and still rank in search.
Expose your data and capabilities through an MCP server. It is the new business development.
Build a product so good your users do the marketing.
